statements.quote: Furthermore, from an exploratory perspective, it is worth noting that higher self‐evaluation was strongly correlated with the perceived usefulness of ChatGPT (see Appendix: median r = 0.34, rbias index = 0.38).
The question is that there was no significant correlation between the self‐evaluation of participants using ChatGPT and their actual performance (see Appendix Tables A1).
First, the perceived usefulness of ChatGPT was strongly correlated with higher self‐evaluation (see Appendix Tables A1, rbias index = 0.38).
Second, perceived task difficulty was positively associated with invested mental effort (see Appendix Tables A1, r = 0.54).

Furthermore, from an exploratory perspective, it is worth noting that actual performance and self‐efficacy (see variables three, four, and five in Appendix Tables A1 and A3) showed an ignorable correlation in the human–ChatGPT group (median: rpre = 0.07, rpost = 0.04).
The datasets used and/or analyzed during the current study are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
Additional supporting information can be found online in the Supporting Information section. Appendix. Supporting document.

notes: The complete 84,429-character markdown conversion was read, including references and the final Supporting Information notice; relevant statements were verified with PyMuPDF text extraction from the 16-page journal PDF. The PDF contains zero embedded files. Quotes preserve source wording and punctuation, with PDF line-wrap hyphens and whitespace normalized and subscript labels rendered as extracted text. No c089 repository URL, code-availability statement, or preregistration link is stated. The form's data_and_code contains no URL, only the on-request statement. The sole explicit data-access route is the corresponding author on reasonable request (p. 13); no request was made. The article DOI and publisher landing page both returned HTTP 403 bot checks. Consequently the external Appendix could not be listed or inspected, and its filenames, file sizes, license, contents beyond the main-text descriptions, and actual access requirements remain unconfirmed. The main text identifies scoring-reference materials and exploratory correlation tables, but that is not evidence of a public participant-level dataset. No relevant public deposit was identified in the named repository searches. Broad searches were refined rather than exhaustively paginated; OSF's named endpoint searches titles and does not establish absence across all of an author's projects. Zenodo initially rejected size=100 with HTTP 400; public size=25 searches succeeded. An ambiguous namesake deposit, https://zenodo.org/records/21922070 (Analysis_code; creator 'zhiwei, liu'), was excluded after HTTP 200 checks of its landing page, https://zenodo.org/api/records/21922070, and https://zenodo.org/api/records/21922070/files/Analysis_Code.zip/content. The API lists one file, Analysis_Code.zip, 41021 bytes, CC BY 4.0; the ZIP's 10 entries comprise five Python scripts, four archived summary JSON files, and a README. The script code/monai_extended_audit.py explicitly concerns a locked uterine leiomyoma test cohort. It is unrelated to c089 and is not counted in deposits. The archive was read only in memory and no downloaded file was saved or executed. With no confirmed public c089 dataset, no participant rows, arm columns, outcome scores, or complete idea texts could be inspected. Public data therefore cannot currently resolve the form's peer-arm people-to-score mapping, analyzed-person counts, or individual baseline handling, compute new pairwise tests or participant-level SEs, or establish possible overlap with c471. The external appendix open item remains unresolved. Overall confidence is medium because the on-request statement is explicit but the publisher supplement was inaccessible and deposit discovery is not exhaustive. Task materials are printed in Table 2 and Figure 1, and Figure 3 supplies selected examples; these do not provide participant-linked outcomes or a complete response corpus.
